newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power up despite nuke talk.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power up despite nuke talk.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic rose Tuesday despite talk of an early return of a large regional nuclear power unit from refueling, market sources said.

"The market has taken off," said one East Coast broker, adding the climb in bulk power prices in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool were triggered by higher October natural gas and fuel oil prices.
However, power demand in the midsection of the eastern seaboard remained tepid due to cool weather. "The rate of dispatch is about the same," one PJM trader said.

The 1,100 megawatt (MW) Peachbottom 2 nuclear unit in Delta, Pa., was already in startup mode late Monday, two weeks earlier than expected, according to Tuesday's Nuclear Regulatory Commission's daily status report.
The station was shut Sept 13 for a 30-day refueling and maintenance outage.
PECO Energy Co, the operator of Peachbottom, could not immediately be reached for comment about the status of the unit.
Talk of more generating capacity would usually depress prices, but higher fuel costs overrode concerns about Peachbottom 2 early return to operation, market sources said.

Firm electricity prices for heavy load hours on Wednesday in PJM were quoted at $20.00-$$20.75 a megawatt hour (MWh), up from Monday's range of $20.25-$20.50. Next-day peak deals were reported done at $20.00, $20.35 and $20.60.
Firm PJM electricity for Wednesday's light load hours was pegged at $15.00-$15.75, compared with Monday's quote near $15.00 for Tuesday.
PJM power for the rest of the week was assessed at $20.00-$21.00, wider than a quote of $20.00-$20.50 on Monday. An unconfirmed transacted was heard done at $20.50.
Peak, firm PJM electricity for the balance of October was valued at $20.25-$20.60, up from Monday's $20.20-$20.40.
November PJM was quoted at $22.25-$22.50, higher than Monday's $21.75-$21.90 range.

December firm, peak PJM was valued at $26.25-$26.50, up from a quote of $25.70-$25.90 on Monday. PJM electricity for the fourth quarter of 1996 was quoted $23.00-$23.50, also higher than Monday's $22.30-$22.50.
January/February 1997 PJM electricity was valued at $30.00-$30.50, up from $29.50-$29.70 on Monday.
